nate: Morning — first day. Fedora 38 laptop, NetworkManager WireGuard profile from IT (split tunnel). Trying to `curl https://registry.internal.redwood/v2/` and `git clone git@github.internal.redwood:team/repo.git` both fail with TLS handshake / certificate mismatch. Public github and public curl works. Any tips?

infra-jen: welcome! Quick checks: `resolvectl status`, `cat /etc/resolv.conf`, and `wg show` (you can redact keys). Also paste the exact curl output (error lines). Could be DNS search domain or stub resolver returning the wrong IP.

nate: copies below. `resolvectl status` (trimmed):
```
Global: DNSSEC=no
Link 3 (wg0):
    Current Scopes: DNS
    LLMNR setting: no
    MulticastDNS setting: no
    DNSSEC setting: no
    DNS Servers: 10.40.0.2
    DNS Domain: ~internal.redwood

Link 2 (wlan0):
    DNS Servers: 192.168.1.1
```
`cat /etc/resolv.conf` shows the systemd stub and search domain: `search redwood.com`

Curl output: `curl: (60) SSL: certificate subject name '*.redwood-public.com' does not match 'registry.internal.redwood'`

dig against the WG DNS: `dig @10.40.0.2 registry.internal.redwood +short` returns `10.40.5.12`. But `dig registry.internal.redwood +short` returns `35.190.23.11` (our public LB). So system resolver is appending the search domain or using the global stub which rewrites names.

tasha: aha — looks like the search path (redwood.com) is getting appended when the resolver uses the stub, so `registry.internal.redwood` might be turned into `registry.internal.redwood.redwood.com` and then resolved by public DNS to the public LB that presents the public cert. Quick workarounds: 1) use the FQDN with a trailing dot to bypass search: `curl https://registry.internal.redwood./v2/` 2) temporarily set the connection's DNS domain for wg0 to only `~internal.redwood` (scoped) so the stub responds correctly.

infra-jen: commands you can try:
```
# quick test (trailing dot)
curl -v https://registry.internal.redwood./v2/

# or set a per-link domain (does not persist across NM reconnects)
resolvectl domain wg0 '~internal.redwood'

# persist via NetworkManager (replace <profile>):
nmcli connection modify <wg-profile> ipv4.dns-search "" ipv4.dns "10.40.0.2"
nmcli connection up <wg-profile>
```
Note: `resolvectl` syntax with `~` scopes the domain to that link so systemd-resolved will prefer the wg link for queries under that domain.

nate: tried the trailing dot — curl returned the registry API JSON immediately. Nice. `git clone` still hits the public host because SSH uses the OS resolver differently; I added an /etc/hosts entry for `git.github.internal.redwood 10.40.6.7` for now.

tasha: for SSH you can also add a Host entry in `~/.ssh/config`:
```
Host github.internal.redwood
  HostName git.github.internal.redwood.
  ProxyCommand none
```
Or use `GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -F ~/.ssh/config' git clone ...` if needed.

infra-jen: creating INF-1301: "systemd-resolved search path causes internal host resolution leak for new hires" assigned to eng-infra. We'll update the WireGuard onboarding profile to set scoped domains and add a note in the new-hires network checklist.

vpn-bot: INF-1301 created and assigned to eng-infra. Priority: P3.

nate: thanks all — trailing-dot trick unblocks me and I'll add these steps to the onboarding notes under "DNS + split tunnel". Appreciate the quick help! :wave:
